Control leases are time-bound and the WebUI repository is in memory, so neither can hold a pin today; until that row lands, arbora carries pins in the engine-backed interim carrier (EgPinStore, kind arbora.fleet.pin, far-future expiry, fresh lease id per put) and the live-engine L4 proof stays in the medulla specs.

decisions: EgPinStore writes through the service-authorized engine client's control leases (the same wiring the served invocation composes for EgPlanStore; no second database). put is a no-op on the same binding, revokes and re-issues under a fresh lease id on a changed binding; delete is a lease revocation; list_tenant pages the tenant-wide kind list (limit clamped 1..100).

decisions: fleet.tools.pin and fleet.tools.unpin are MANAGE/WRITE/mcp:delegate/EVENT/MCP-only ops beside FleetUnloadParams; FleetUnloadParams gains include_pinned; visible_names calls restore_pins before revoke_invisible; FLEET_OPERATIONS and RESIDENT_NAMES stay as they are (10 resident tools).

MultiplexerOps.pin resolves each item inline with stable codes (missing item -> NOT_FOUND; policy outage -> POLICY_UNAVAILABLE; denial -> POLICY_DENIED), so a pin is never wider than a load by the same caller. restore_pins repeats the check with the caller's current scopes and policy and suspends without deleting. A call to a pinned tool takes the fleet.call path with the caller's own delegated credential; the durable record stores the binding only.

Stable codes: SCOPE_REQUIRED without mcp:delegate; NOT_FOUND for a missing or not-loadable item; INVALID_ARGUMENT for empty or oversize items (1..32); POLICY_DENIED and POLICY_UNAVAILABLE from the policy decision; UNAVAILABLE when the PinStore is unreachable (a store failure pins nothing and leaves the live session unchanged); LOAD_CAP_EXCEEDED with cap=pinned and the pinned list. unpin of an item that is not pinned succeeds and reports it under not_pinned. LoadCapExceeded gains a cap field (pinned or session); the code table stays ArboraErrorCode, no code is new.

decisions: The served L4 drives the real manage and ask intent tools over the MCP registration, with GovernedSessionVisibility restoring the pins after a rebuild. The harness uses a session cap of 128: with the default cap of 64 no single 70-item load can succeed alongside two pinned items (72 > 64), so a larger configured cap is what makes the row's scenario reachable; a second 70-item load then forces real LRU eviction. The 70-item group is loaded one item per clock tick so LRU is time-ordered (a batched load marks every item with one clock reading).

decisions: Coverage gate: the workspace.yml connectors group (the human-edited manifest outranks the deployed MCP config) is compared against the enabled fleet endpoints and the admitted catalog's tool counts. The check is pure, reads no clock, and never auto-disables, skips or hides an offender.

Frozen RegisteredConnector{repo, server} and CoverageReport{registered, covered, missing, zero_tools, ok} in arbora/fleet/coverage.py. registered_connectors reads the connectors group of platform_config_file('workspace.yml'): plain repo strings or mappings with repo (+ optional mcp_server), default server = repo name; self-served connectors excluded; a missing or unparsable file, a bad entry or a duplicate server key raises FleetCoverageError (fail-closed); a parsable manifest without the group registers nothing.

check_fleet_coverage(registered, endpoints, tool_counts, unadmitted) is pure; the reason vocabulary is closed {no_endpoint, not_admitted}; tool_counts comes from the new FleetCatalog.tool_counts(), which reads the sources only (no caller, no child spawn) and counts admitted tool items per server, starting no child. A server with no endpoint is no_endpoint; one that is unadmitted or absent from the admitted catalog is not_admitted; one whose admitted catalog holds no tool item is zero_tools.
The report keeps the registry order the caller passed in; the registry reader itself returns a stable order.

MultiplexerOps.status adds a coverage block built by check_fleet_coverage (the registry and endpoint defaults read the workspace manifest and the deployed config, self-served excluded; an unreadable registry degrades to a registry_unreadable block in non-strict status only). FleetStatusParams gains require_full_coverage; the strict handler pops it before delegating to ops.status (it is a handler-level strict flag, not an op param).
The operator command arbora-production-ops check-fleet-coverage sits beside onboard-fleet in production_ops: engine-backed, prints the report, exits non-zero when ok is false.

A registered connector with no enabled endpoint reports missing with reason no_endpoint; one that is registered but not admitted reports not_admitted; one with zero admitted tools reports zero_tools. The strict status call returns UNAVAILABLE (HTTP 503) naming every offender: the details carry the missing {server, reason} list (reason from the closed vocabulary) and the zero_tools list, and never list a healthy server. The check must not auto-disable, skip or hide an offender.

Served proof over MCP with require_full_coverage true and a fixture workspace.yml of four connectors: three connectors with tools pass; the fourth is first absent (no_endpoint), then admitted with zero tools (zero_tools). The status call refuses each time and names the fourth; after it serves one tool the call succeeds. A delta prompt row shows the offenders to the caller.

CatalogItem.group (in public()) is filled by the catalog builder from the tool metadata key scion/upstream, field namespace, and left unset when the key is absent; a group is a lowercase word of 2 to 24 letters and digits (strict [a-z0-9]{2,24} else unset). FleetCatalog.group_items plus a groups filter on search (an empty query with groups is a browse); groups gained on FleetCatalogParams, FleetLoadParams and FleetUnloadParams.

A load by group resolves to the admitted tool items of the group that the caller may already load, then follows the same path as an item load; it is atomic (the whole group or none) and refuses with the existing LoadCapExceeded when the group would pass the session cap (default 64, hard cap 256 - a group of about 170 tools fits only a session cap above 170). An unknown group yields an empty result, not an error; a load with neither items nor groups is refused INVALID_ARGUMENT by the handler.

An unload by group removes the loaded items of the group and skips pinned items (include_pinned names them under skipped_pinned); an explicit items unload of a pinned item also deletes the durable store record (a pin is fully ended by an explicit unload; selector unloads keep it).
FLEET_GROUP_INVALID (HTTP 400) via _require_valid_groups on invalid group forms; no new knob - the session cap stays as it is.
